validated_results.title: Alcohol intake, drinking patterns, and prostate cancer risk and mortality: a 30-year prospective cohort study of Finnish twins.
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort study investigating midlife alcohol intake and incident prostate cancer risk in Finnish twins.

sample_size.excerpt: N=11,352 participants had data on average alcohol consumption category.
sample_size.location: MATERIALS AND METHODS, Study population, paragraph 1

cases.excerpt: Over the study period, 601 incident cases of prostate cancer and 110 deaths from prostate cancer occurred.

effect_size.excerpt: Exclusion of abstainers did not influence the relative risk estimate (data not shown). Modeling average weekly alcohol consumption as a categorical variable, we found a positive association with prostate cancer risk among moderate (HR 1.20; 95% CI, 0.99, 1.46) and heavy drinkers (HR 1.46; 95% CI, 1.12, 1.91) compared to light drinkers in multivariable models ( Table 2 ).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Compared to light drinkers (≤3 drinks/week; non-abstainers), heavy drinkers (>14 drinks/week) were at a 1.46-fold higher risk (HR 1.46; 95% CI, 1.12, 1.91) of prostate cancer, adjusting for important confounders.

comparison.excerpt: Compared to light drinkers (≤3 drinks/week; non-abstainers), heavy drinkers (>14 drinks/week)

design.excerpt: We aimed to prospectively investigate the association between midlife alcohol intake and drinking patterns with future prostate cancer risk and mortality in a population-based cohort of Finnish twins.

timing.excerpt: Alcohol intake, drinking patterns, and prostate cancer risk and mortality: A 30-year prospective cohort study of Finnish twins

continent.excerpt: Data were drawn from the Older Finnish Twin Cohort and included 11,372 twins followed from 1981 to 2012.
